questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter traffic, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal for drivers 21 or older to drive?

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of your surroundings. Watch the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle. This helps you spot problems early so you can change speed or position.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound your horn loudly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: Use a loud horn blast if a child or pedestrian is about to run into the street in front of your vehicle. This alerts them to danger.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead.
Keep instrument panel lights bright to be visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlight beam.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night because you cannot see as far. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: If about to be hit from behind, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, press yourself against your seat and keep your head on the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Traffic is merging ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic may merge from another road.

questions.question: When must you give the right-of-way to pedestrians?

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
When crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing any street in marked or unmarked crosswalks. Always yield for pedestrian safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
Road construction area.
The road narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a dangerous hill or downgrade ahead. It may be long, steep, or have sharp curves.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. You must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles with a green light.

questions.question: You are in the left of two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. If the driver behind you wants to go faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Drive onto the left shoulder.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for faster driving, passing, and turning left. Use the right lane for slower driving, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for work zones.
Only slow down if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving safely through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers.

questions.question: A rear-facing child restraint system is required for any child:

options.text: Weighing 25 pounds or less.
Age one year or older, weighing 30 pounds or less.
Under one year old, weighing 20 pounds or less.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under one year old, weighing 20 pounds or less.
questions.explanation: State law requires all children under 16 to use proper child restraints in vehicles. A rear-facing child restraint is required for children under one year old who weigh 20 pounds or less.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed of traffic, signal, and then:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right of way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to completely clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, signal, and merge when safe. Watch other traffic closely. Do not expect other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep going.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If the road is covered with heavy smoke, slow down immediately, move as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some types of smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or health.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to pass the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: Make room for cars entering the freeway by:

options.text: Slowing down.
Moving to a different lane.
Keeping your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Create space for entering vehicles by moving to the next lane if possible. If you cannot move, adjust your speed to let them enter safely.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right and stop before entering the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, pull right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, pull right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing, then move right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Right when rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when rain starts.
questions.explanation: The first 30 minutes of rain is most dangerous. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road, making it extremely slippery. Use extra caution on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that people may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas and do not use the brakes. Wait until your tires grip the road again before turning or stopping.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and braking gently. Pull off the road safely when you can.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: Steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left to straighten the car.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the roadway edge, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.
Turn back onto the roadway immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.
questions.explanation: Slow down and check traffic. When it is safe, gradually steer back onto the road. Do not turn sharply or immediately.
